summary.text: 友 combines two hand forms, 又, traditionally associated with friendship. The character means “friend” or “companion”; the hands’ precise contribution and whether they also cue the sound remain debated.

formation.text: 友 is a disputed semantic or phono-semantic compound. The two 又 forms are identified as hands and linked with friendship; one account also assigns 又 a phonetic role. The evidence does not determine whether one or both forms provide that sound cue.

components.text: 又 depicts a hand. In 友, two such forms are described as facing the same way and sometimes joined, supporting a two-hands interpretation. Some accounts treat them as semantic; another also gives 又 a phonetic role, but its placement is unresolved.

sound_limitation.text: Old Chinese comparisons make a phonetic contribution plausible but do not identify whether one or both repeated 又 forms provide it. The modern Mandarin resemblance alone does not establish an ancient sound role.

sound.text: The Mandarin readings are similar, but that modern resemblance alone does not establish an ancient sound relationship.
The Middle Chinese reconstructions are similar, with different tone categories.
In this reconstruction, the forms share initial and most rhyme material but differ in the final element, making a phonetic connection plausible without proving the component’s role.

history.text: Oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, and small-seal forms are reported. Early forms are described as two similarly oriented hands, sometimes joined; in small seal the forms are arranged vertically. This records changes in layout, without establishing a particular scene of cooperation.
The received Shuowen explanation connects the two 又 forms with people who share aims and interact as friends. This is a traditional interpretation of the graph.

uncertainties.text: Accounts differ on whether the two 又 forms contribute meaning alone or also sound. Sound comparisons support a possible phonetic role but do not determine which repeated form has which function.

The earliest reported contexts include a personal name and a sacrificial use read as 侑. The evidence does not establish “friend” as the earliest attested sense or a continuous path from those early uses to later friend and associate uses.
A Mawangdui manuscript is reported to use 友 to write 柔, “soft.” This is a separate use of the whole graph for another word; the supplied account does not establish the sound basis for the borrowing.

limitations.text: The attested uses do not establish a chronological or semantic bridge among the early name, sacrificial, friend, associate, verbal, and other listed uses; no development between them is asserted.

relationships.text: The two 又 forms are interpreted as hands contributing the idea of friendship, though the intended scene is uncertain.
Each 又 is identified as a hand form, and the graph brings two such forms together. This describes the imagery without asserting a literal scene of cooperation.
